scope: Fabric FF, CCU2 and output-selection research; not emulator execution or silicon validation

rules.claim: REGn.SD=1 selects the local DI path; SD=0 selects M. nextpnr pairs a COMB F driver for SD=1 or renames DI to M for SD=0.
DI is reached from the selected F output via fixed F# -> DI# -> DI#_SLICE connections, rather than a second independent copy of the LUT output.
Each FF has separate REGSET, SD and LSRMODE settings; the two FF of a slice share GSR, CEMUX and selected CLK/LSR wires.
Two raw CLK and two raw LSR routes have inversion/mode controls. MUXCLK0..3 and MUXLSR0..3 select the slice inputs. nextpnr applies additional tile-wide compatibility rules.
Public FD1P3IX/JX documentation gives synchronous local clear/preset precedence over enable. TRELLIS_FF has local LSR precedence over CE in both synchronous and asynchronous branches.
TRELLIS_FF preload takes its reset value from M; the software event list samples it on LSR assertion or an active clock edge, not every change of M while asynchronous LSR remains asserted.
TRELLIS_FF has no global-reset input or GSR behavior despite its GSR parameter. Startup observations and identical GSR parameter traces cannot validate physical startup or GSR.

Database defaults and synthesis defaults differ: PLC REGSET defaults to SET and SD to 1; TRELLIS_FF defaults to RESET, and the writer defaults SD to 0. Raw CRAM constraints remain authoritative for decoding.

Yosys lattice_gsr resolves AUTO using presence of a GSR/SGSR primitive and the nogsr cell attribute. It can remove matching asynchronous local reset wiring; this is a netlist transformation, not runtime GSR emulation.
For each CCU2 half p=INIT[ABCD], g=INIT[AB]; S=p XOR (INJECT1=NO ? carry : 0), next=p ? carry : (INJECT1=NO ? g : 0). The second half uses the first half's carry.
INJECT1=YES does not force carry to zero when p=1: carry propagates, although the sum ignores it. INIT low four bits feed both LUT4 and LUT2 functions.
Eight INJECT1 settings overlap F-output route bits. LOGIC mux selection and CCU2 injection cannot be executed as independent simultaneous meanings of the same CRAM bit.

The current Yosys latch synthesis probe uses LUT feedback rather than a fabric FF latch configuration. This does not establish the configuration binding of the level-sensitive registers mentioned by the datasheet.

nextpnr uses CCU2C cells for fabric carry feed-in, feed-out and loopback, consuming ordinary carry/LUT resources. With unused C/D inputs high, their public-model functions are COUT=A0 for INIT0=000a/INIT1=ffff, NO/YES; and S0=CIN, looped COUT=CIN for INIT0=0000/INIT1=000a, NO/NO.
TRELLIS_FF software always captures DI and has no SD parameter; post-pack SD=0 data on M needs a separate adapter. M retains its separate preload role.

open_questions.question: Physical startup/PUR versus user GSR, disabled slice GSR, REGSET and PRLD initialization; assertion/release interaction with local controls and global synchronizer.
Does asynchronous PRLD follow M continuously while LSR is asserted, or sample on specific events? Which combinations of SD, PRLD and shared M are physically meaningful?
Verify DI/M data selection and shared CE/CLK/LSR/GSR with paired FF and wide-LUT mux use, distinguishing physical constraints from placer conservatism.
Establish mode-qualified F/OFX/carry outputs, injection codes, noncanonical MODE patterns and chain entry/exit at missing PLC neighbors; empty route patterns alone are insufficient.
Define digital unknown/contending-control semantics and simultaneous-event policy without treating Verilog if/X scheduling as a physical-chip guarantee.
Find a physical configuration binding for the datasheet's level-sensitive registers; LUT-feedback latch synthesis does not identify that binding.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Build distinguishable REGSET 0/1 fingerprints with user GSR enabled/disabled, then exercise configuration startup and GSR assertion/release with clocks stopped and running. Keep observer outside the reset under test.
hardware_cases.observe: Initial Q and retention, differences between startup and user GSR, selected global synchronizer and local LSR priority; record exact CRAM.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Constrain DI and M separately; sweep SD and PRLD, both clock/reset polarities and CE constants. Hold asynchronous LSR active while changing M without clock edges, then add an active edge.
hardware_cases.observe: Continuous versus sampled preload, normal data source and shared-M compatibility; distinguish open-model sampling from hardware.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Pair FF0/1 in each slice with asymmetric REGSET/SD/LSRMODE and shared controls; combine wide-LUT mux use in separate variants. Change reset and CE away from edges before separate coincidence tests.
hardware_cases.observe: Shared versus individual behavior and physical availability of routed paths; save constraints and routes.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Use one-hot and asymmetric CCU2 INIT, all injection pairs, both CIN values, FF observation and wide-LUT alternatives. Test local chain stages and cross-PLC boundary positions separately; include exact route-bit manifests.
hardware_cases.observe: S0/S1/COUT and active F/OFX paths per MODE; distinguish injection from ordinary output mux selection. Undefined patterns retain undocumented status.

hardware_cases.stimulus: After finding a candidate physical latch configuration, hold each gate level and change D without edges; compare with an explicitly LUT-feedback latch.
hardware_cases.observe: Transparency and hold behavior plus resource/configuration binding; do not substitute a feedback implementation for evidence of a register latch.
